messages.subject: For Laura Exner | Executive Leadership, Sustainability & Global Stakeholder Strategy | Proposal
messages.body:
Dear Ms. Exner,

I am writing from Guyana, where I serve as Liaison Director, Social Responsibility at AGM Inc., part of Zijin Mining Group. My role spans ESG, government relations, regulatory coordination, corporate affairs, stakeholder strategy and executive issue management in a complex multinational industrial environment.

Höegh Autoliners' global operating model, leadership-development agenda and transition toward lower-emission shipping strongly align with the kind of cross-functional leadership work I handle today. My experience is strongest where external expectations, public institutions, sustainability commitments and executive execution need to be connected through one disciplined operating framework.

I prepared a Höegh Autoliners-specific Strategic Value Creation Proposal rather than sending a conventional CV alone. It sets out where I would add value across executive stakeholder strategy, responsible growth, sustainability governance and international market engagement. My three-page Executive CV forms the final section.

I am open to relocation to Norway and employer-supported work authorization. My strongest fit would be a Director, Head, Country, Regional or senior leadership mandate across Sustainability, External Affairs, Corporate Affairs, Government Relations, Strategic Partnerships or stakeholder-facing transformation.

I would value a short confidential conversation. If another senior leader owns the most relevant mandate, I would be grateful if you would route the proposal internally.

Kind regards,
Ragunauth Ramsaroop
Liaison Director, Social Responsibility
AGM Inc. | Zijin Mining Group
ragunauthramsaroop@icloud.com
ragunauthramsaroop.com

strategic_brief.title: Strategic Value Creation Proposal: Executive Stakeholder Strategy, Sustainability and Global Market Leadership
strategic_brief.executive_summary: Höegh Autoliners operates a global shipping network while pursuing growth, leadership development and a transition toward lower-emission transport. That combination requires senior leaders who can work across cultures, functions and jurisdictions while keeping stakeholder trust, sustainability commitments and business execution aligned. I bring director-level experience from a multinational resource company where government relations, ESG, regulatory coordination, corporate affairs and executive issue management are integrated into daily operations. My strongest value would be in connecting external affairs, sustainability, people and operating priorities through disciplined stakeholder intelligence, commitment governance and executive follow-through across complex markets.
strategic_brief.company_context: Höegh Autoliners is headquartered in Oslo and operates globally across deep-sea RoRo transportation. Its careers material emphasizes an international workforce, leadership development, cross-border assignments and career progression into senior management. The company also positions greener and more sustainable shipping as a strategic priority. This creates a strong need for leaders who are comfortable at the intersection of external institutions, sustainability obligations, internal operating teams and international market development. In multinational settings, risks often emerge first through regulatory changes, public expectations, stakeholder concerns or gaps between corporate commitments and local execution. A structured approach to these interfaces can improve leadership visibility, strengthen reputation and support more consistent execution across markets.

opportunities.title: Global stakeholder intelligence
opportunities.rationale: International shipping is exposed to regulators, port authorities, customers, governments and community expectations across multiple jurisdictions. Material issues can develop locally before they are visible in corporate reporting or central decision processes.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would build a concise stakeholder-intelligence system that ranks issues by materiality, assigns ownership and connects external developments to leadership decisions, communications and operating priorities.

opportunities.title: Sustainability commitment governance
opportunities.rationale: Transition commitments become more credible when targets are linked to accountable owners, source evidence, milestones and closure records. Without that discipline, sustainability programs can become disconnected from operational decision-making.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would establish practical commitment governance that links sustainability objectives and external promises to responsible functions, evidence requirements, management review and measurable follow-through.

opportunities.title: Cross-functional executive coordination
opportunities.rationale: Complex global issues rarely sit within one function. Sustainability, regulatory, people, commercial and reputation risks often overlap, making fast coordination and clear escalation essential for senior management.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would create an executive issue-management rhythm that brings together relevant functions, clarifies decisions and maintains one view of high-priority external and operating matters.

opportunities.title: International growth and external affairs
opportunities.rationale: Growth across international markets is stronger when commercial strategy is supported by disciplined engagement with institutions, regulators and strategic partners. This is particularly important in emerging markets where infrastructure, policy and stakeholder expectations evolve quickly.
opportunities.how_i_can_help: I would support market-entry and growth priorities with government engagement, stakeholder mapping, regulatory coordination and strategic partnership development grounded in direct emerging-market experience.

days_0_30: Map priority stakeholder, sustainability and regulatory interfaces across selected markets.
Identify recurring executive issues where ownership or escalation is fragmented.
days_31_60: Introduce a pilot stakeholder-intelligence and commitments framework.
Align selected sustainability and external-affairs priorities with accountable internal owners.
days_61_90: Use live market and stakeholder issues to test the framework and improve executive visibility.
Deliver a concise dashboard covering commitments, emerging issues and required management decisions.
days_91_180: Scale the approach across additional markets or functions.
Measure performance through issue closure, stakeholder outcomes, assurance readiness and reduced execution surprises.

potential_impact: Earlier visibility of material stakeholder and regulatory developments across international markets.
Stronger accountability behind sustainability and responsible-growth commitments.
Faster cross-functional resolution of external and reputational issues.
Improved alignment between market growth, stakeholder trust and executive execution.
background_relevance: Director-level experience across ESG, corporate affairs, government relations, regulatory coordination, social performance and executive advisory in a multinational industrial setting.
Experience coordinating ministries, regulators and internal operating functions around complex external commitments and business priorities.
Direct exposure to renewable-energy governance, carbon-data traceability and responsible-business evidence in a regulated operation.
International management exposure through multinational-company structures, executive engagement and cross-cultural stakeholder work.
